A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ME2/TRM research and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–K. Added subsections and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original preference-evaluation, Best-of-N, and reinforcement-learning results, including 88.6% TRM validation accuracy in Table 1 and appendix ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a 400-pair human/LLM reliability study and larger-generator Best-of-N results in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The DAG construction and abstraction pipeline, pairwise preference procedure, Bradley–Terry-trained TRM, and gated GRPO reward remain unchanged. Corrected prompt headings leave their substantive instructions intact.

E1.justification: Training sources and benchmark tasks are retained. The reliability study samples existing preference pairs, and the larger-generator experiment uses the already evaluated AIME25. These additions change settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix G.4 adds Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and human experts as reference judgments compared with the constructed preference labels. Existing PRM, PromptOnly, and verifier comparator sets remain; Table 5 abbreviates the retained PRM names.

E3.justification: New settings include a 400-pair audit with three human experts and three LLM judges, reporting accuracy after excluding ties. Appendix G.6 adds GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen3-235B-A22B as evaluation generators under the existing Best-of-N protocol. Original experiment settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G.4 adds a targeted check of whether preference labels reflect DeepSeek-V3.2-specific judge bias, using independent human and model annotations. The original weighting-coefficient ablation, training-dynamics analysis, and reasoning case studies are retained.

E5.justification: New cost accounting in G.5 states four orderings, while retained Appendix F specifies three evaluations for each of two orders. This adds inconsistent repetition information without establishing an actual run-count change. The five-repeat test-time protocol and existing uncertainty displays remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports non-tie agreement of 86.3%, 93.0%, 89.8%, and 90.0% for Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and humans. Table 5 adds TRM AIME25 accuracy of 86.7% and 78.7% at N=16 for GPT-OSS-120B and Qwen3-235B-A22B. Original results remain unchanged, including the ablation renumbered from Table 4 to Table 6.

T1.justification: The reward-shaping and policy-improvement theorems, proofs in Appendices A–B, and Bradley–Terry formulation are unchanged. G.5's O(n)-to-O(d+b) attachment-pool argument already appeared in Appendix E of v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same framework, reasoning-quality optimization claims, and headline gains of up to 19.3% at test time and 3.9% during RL. New studies add support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: G.4 interprets independent agreement as evidence against judge-specific artifacts; G.5 explains cost amortization; G.6 attributes smaller gains to stronger generators. Its claim of consistent outperformance is overstated: Table 5 includes ties and a GPT-OSS-120B N=2 loss to ReasonFlux-PRM, 81.3% versus 82.0%.

D1.justification: G.5 newly details offline processing and costs, including approximately 180K traces, fewer than 12B DeepSeek-V3.2 tokens, and roughly $5K total. These document the existing pipeline. The stated code/data repository changes from zzzhr97/TRM to Simplified-Reasoning/TRM; original training details remain.

R1.justification: Cited works and substantive positioning against prior reasoning-structure and reward-modeling research are retained. Changes to the GPQA and Reinforce++ bibliography entries concern publication metadata, not different works or research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds three Appendix G subsections and corresponding cross-references, acknowledgements, and updated author/contact/publication text. It also corrects several headings and grammatical phrases. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds two tables and relocates the unchanged ablation as Table 6. Figure 3 is redrawn, Figure 4's fractional-accuracy axis label and panel-description caption are corrected, and appendix prompt labels are fixed. Existing displays also shift within the retained layout.

improvement.justification: Independent human/LLM validation strengthens label credibility beyond v1's same-judge checks; larger-generator results and construction-cost disclosure add useful evidence about applicability and feasibility. Caption corrections improve clarity. These benefits outweigh the limited new defects—the inconsistent ordering count and overstated Table 5 interpretation—but support a modest overall improvement.
